title: Open WebUI OAuth token exchange -- T1528 raw provider token accepted with no audience check
author: WinstonRedGuard -- sigma plugin observed rules (derived from breach corpus)
description:
Vendor-disclosed detection for CVE-2026-70482 (GHSA-rq84-p6rr-vf89,
CVSS 8.1 HIGH), affecting Open WebUI from 0.8.0 until 0.11.0.

When `ENABLE_OAUTH_TOKEN_EXCHANGE=True`,
`/oauth/{provider}/token/exchange` accepted a raw OAuth provider access
token and validated it by calling the provider's userinfo endpoint --
WITHOUT confirming which OAuth CLIENT the token was originally issued
to. Any party holding an access token minted for ANY client registered
with the same provider -- including applications the Open WebUI
operator never authorized and does not control -- could exchange that
token for a live Open WebUI session as the token's owner. This is a
classic audience-confusion bug: the endpoint checks "is this token
valid for this provider" instead of "was this token issued to MY
client".

This corpus already carries `observed_librechat_mcp_oauth_resource_mismatch_t1528`
for a similarly-shaped OAuth trust bug in a different product; that one
is a resource-metadata redirect, this one is missing audience/client
validation on token exchange -- distinct mechanisms, same
broader class of "the OAuth trust boundary was assumed rather than
checked".

Detection logic flags a token-exchange request whose provider userinfo
response succeeds but whose token was NOT issued to Open WebUI's own
registered client id -- the exact check the vulnerable endpoint skipped.

Aggregated from 1 first-party vendor security advisory (open-webui, via
GHSA and NVD, citing both fix commits), fixed in 0.11.0.
